# Tool index — every callable in `Tools_code/`

249 functions across 38 modules. Signature and one line each.

This is the complete list, so a tool you cannot find here does not exist.
For the full explanation of any one of them:

```bash
python Tool_scripts/tool_help.py apply_chain
```

Read that before the first time you call anything. The one line below is
enough to know a tool exists and roughly what it is for; it is not enough
to call it correctly.

## `bake`

Low-poly + UV + texture baking. Not specific to any model.

- `stash_cage(obj_name, cage_name)` — Copy `obj_name` aside as the low-poly cage, hidden, no modifiers.
- `show(obj_name, visible=True)` — Show or hide an object in the viewport AND the render.
- `unwrap(obj_name, angle_limit=66.0, island_margin=0.02, method='SMART')` — UV the object. Returns (islands, uv_area, faces).
- `cylindrical_uv(obj_name, uv_name='CylindricalUV', axis=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), front_direction=(0.0, -1.0, 0.0), right_direction=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0), axis_origin=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), axis_min=None, axis_max=None, replace=True, space='LOCAL')` — Assign a deliberate cylindrical UV layer around an arbitrary axis.
- `uv_stats(obj_name)` — (islands, coverage 0-1, faces). Islands counted by connected UV vertices, which is what a packer means by an island.
- `uv_layout_png(obj_name, path, size=1024, line=(1.0, 0.85, 0.2))` — Draw the UV islands to a PNG, so the layout can be looked at.
- `new_image(name, size=2048, colorspace='Non-Color', fill=(0, 0, 0, 1), float_buffer=False)` — Create a square image to bake into, replacing any of the same name.
- `save_image(image_name, path)` — Write a baked image to `path` as PNG, creating parent dirs.
- `load_image(path, colorspace='sRGB')` — Load an image file, reusing it if already loaded.
- `multiply_images(a_name, b_name, out_name, out_path, b_gain=1.0, b_floor=0.0, tint=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0))` — out = a * clamp(b * gain, floor, 1) * tint, saved as sRGB.
- `tile_from_crop(src_path, out_path, x, y, size, mirror=True, colorspace='sRGB')` — Cut a square out of a photographed texture and make it tile.
- `image_stats(image_name)` — (mean, min, max) of RGB — the cheapest proof a bake produced anything other than the fill colour it started as.
- `ensure_material(obj_name, mat_name)` — Give the object exactly one node-based material, named `mat_name`.
- `set_bake_target(obj_name, image_name, mat_name=None)` — Point the object's material at `image_name` as the bake destination.
- `bake(low_name, image_name, high_name=None, bake_type='NORMAL', samples=16, cage_extrusion=0.06, max_ray_distance=0.0, margin=16, pass_filter=None, device='CPU')` — Bake `bake_type` onto `low_name`'s active image.

## `boolean_ops`

Apply ordered Boolean differences without repeating Blender context boilerplate.

- `apply_boolean_differences(obj_name, cutter_names, solver='EXACT', modifier_prefix='difference', delete_cutters=True)` — Apply ordered DIFFERENCE modifiers for named disposable cutters.

## `checkpoint`

Per-step .blend checkpoints, so a rewind does not re-execute earlier steps.

- `path_for(run_name, step)` — Return the absolute checkpoint path for ``run_name`` and ``step``.
- `save_step(run_name, step)` — Write the scene as it stands at the end of `step`.
- `load_step(run_name, step)` — Restore the scene to the end of `step`. Keeps the current window layout.
- `latest_before(run_name, step)` — Highest checkpointed step strictly below `step`, or None.

## `cleanup`

Return Blender to an empty scene between tasks, without touching the window.

- `reset_scene(*, keep_camera=False)` — Empty the scene and free its data. Returns what was removed.

## `fracture`

Cracks that read as SPLIT STONE rather than as an engraved line.

- `profile(keys)` — (t, value) keyframes -> the callable apply_stroke(profile=) wants.
- `plan(points, region, ppm, seed=0, core_r=0.028, waviness='jagged', amplitude=0.004, roughness=1.3, smooth=False, shoulder=None, lobes=())` — Resolve the core path and everything derived from it.
- `preview_strokes(pl, region, ppm, core_r, shoulder=None, at=0.36)` — Stroke dicts for paint.stroke_lines_preview, drawn from the PLAN.
- `cut(obj_name, points, region, ppm, seed=0, core_r=0.028, core_strength=0.85, core_profile=FRACTURE, waviness='jagged', amplitude=0.004, roughness=1.3, smooth=False, shoulder=None, lobes=(), label='crack')` — Cut one fracture. Returns {"rows": [...], "plan": {...}}.

## `geom_digest`

Hash the scene's geometry so two runs of the same actions can be compared.

- `resolve(path)` — Absolute path, interpreting a relative one against the harness root.
- `object_digest(obj, *, evaluated=True)` — Hash of one object's evaluated world-space geometry.
- `scene_digest(*, evaluated=True, include_empties=False)` — Digest of every mesh in the scene, ordered by name so it is stable.
- `write_digest(path, *, evaluated=True, note='')` — Compute the scene digest and write it to ``path`` as JSON.
- `compare(before_path, after_path)` — Diff two digest files. Read this from the shell, not from Blender.

## `handle`

Handle-building helpers. Split so each segment is two actions:

- `prepare_segment(label, extrude_t, rotate_deg, n_dots=6, px_step=40)` — Extrude + rotate + render the grab grid for this segment.
- `apply_grab(label, grab_row, grab_col, prepare_action=None)` — Translate the currently-selected face's verts to image (grab_row, grab_col) on the grab grid that `prepare_segment(label, ...)` last wrote.
- `extrude_rotate(label, extrude_t, rotate_deg)` — Extrude + rotate, no grab. For segments where the rotation alone lands the tip where you want (typically the handle's final segment).
- `chain_preview(label='chain', history_points=None)` — Render the currently-selected face's centre as a red dot on a normalized (0-1, top-left origin) coordinate grid overlay.
- `points_plan_preview(world_points, label='points')` — READ-ONLY preview of arbitrary WORLD-SPACE 3D points (not a chain path off the selected face — any points, e.g. proposed vertex targets for a flat patch mesh like the wing) — projects each to screen and draws the same numbered-dot/connecting-line overlay chain_plan_preview uses, via the same overlay script. No geometry is touched.
- `quad_plan_preview(corners, label='quad')` — READ-ONLY preview of a set of vertex moves — each corner drawn in its OWN color, as a hollow circle at its CURRENT position connected by a line to a filled circle at its TARGET position (so it reads as "this vertex moves to there"), plus the targets connected to each other as a closed outline in the given order. No geometry is touched.
- `chain_plan_preview(points, label='chain', scales=None)` — READ-ONLY preview of the whole candidate chain, drawn directly on the current viewport render as numbered dots + connecting lines — no geometry is touched. Computes the exact same step-by-step unprojection apply_chain() would (each point's depth-reference is the PREVIOUS point in the chain, starting from the current selected face's centre), so what you see here is exactly what apply_chain(points) would build.
- `chain_profile_preview(points, label='chain', scales=None)` — READ-ONLY. The chain drawn as a SILHOUETTE: each station as a cross-section tick, plus the rails joining their ends.
- `face_radius_world(face, mw)` — Mean distance from a face's centroid to its verts, in world units — the radius of the ring, for previews that want to draw it.
- `align_seed_face(points, label='align')` — Pre-rotate the currently selected face (around its own centroid) so its normal already points toward `points[0]` — call this ONCE, right before `apply_chain(points, ...)`, ONLY on a genuinely fresh seed face that has no adjacent extruded geometry yet (e.g. a just-separated coincident duplicate face for a new independent limb/branch — see apply_chain's docstring and the finger2/3/4 seed-separate pattern).
- `apply_chain(points, label='chain', auto_face=True, face_mode='average', rotations=None, scales=None)` — Extrude the currently-selected face through a chain of normalized (x_norm, y_norm) points — the same 0-1, top-left-origin grid drawn by `chain_preview()` / `chain_plan_preview()`.
- `apply_body_profile(steps, direction=1, label='profile', pre_scale=1.0)` — Apply a chained extrude+scale-along-local-Z profile — the same `steps`/`pre_scale` `perceive.body_profile_preview(steps, direction, pre_scale)` showed. Mutates the mesh for real. Requires the current end-cap FACE to already be selected (edit mode, face select), same as the preview.

## `landmarks`

Landmarks — name verts so they survive across topology-changing ops.

- `tag(name, description='')` — Tag currently selected verts as a landmark.
- `resolve(name)` — Return the vert INDICES (not BMVerts) belonging to landmark `name`.
- `select(name)` — Deselect all and select the landmark's verts in EDIT mode.
- `select_edges_among(names, bm, exclusive=True)` — Select edges whose BOTH endpoints lie within a SINGLE landmark.

## `lighting`

Camera, lights, backdrop and a real render.

- `config_value(key, default=None)` — Replay config lookup: environment first, then blendcua.env.
- `engine_override()` — Engine forced by config, or None to honour what the action asked for.
- `cycles_device()` — 'CPU' / 'GPU' forced by config, or None to honour the call's prefer_gpu.
- `set_engine(name)` — Set the requested render engine, returning the one actually in effect.
- `aim(obj, target)` — Point `obj`'s -Z axis at `target`. Lights and cameras both.
- `spherical(target, distance, azimuth, elevation)` — A point `distance` from `target`, at that azimuth and elevation.
- `key_light(target, distance, azimuth, elevation, energy, colour=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0), size=0.25, kind='AREA', name='Key', spread=None)` — An aimed light, positioned relative to what it is lighting.
- `world_colour(rgb, strength=1.0)` — A flat world. Deliberately not an HDRI: the reference's background is a plain warm gradient with no environment in it at all, and an HDRI would put reflections of a room onto ten glossy chillies.
- `backdrop(rgb, width=6.0, height=4.0, distance=1.4, z=-1.0, roughness=0.95, name='Backdrop')` — A big matte plane behind the subject.
- `light_frame(light)` — (origin, axis, right, up) of a light, in world space.
- `cut_through(light, point, distance)` — Where a flag's edge must sit for its shadow to fall on `point`.
- `plumb_angle(light, cut, distance)` — The roll, in degrees, that makes a flag's shadow edge VERTICAL.
- `flag(light, cut=0.0, side=1, distance=0.3, size=2.0, angle=0.0, name='Flag')` — A cutter: an opaque plane between a light and its subject, blocking part of the beam so the shadow it throws has a HARD, STRAIGHT edge.
- `point_at_screen(camera, u, v, max_dist=12.0)` — The world point under a normalised screen position (u across, v down).
- `cutter_plane(light, boundary, shadow_point, frac=0.5, width=0.8, height=2.0, tilt=0.0, name='Flag')` — A VERTICAL blocker whose shadow edge passes through `boundary`.
- `camera(target, distance, azimuth, elevation, lens=50.0, name='Camera', dof_fstop=None, shift=(0.0, 0.0))` — A scene camera, aimed. Made active.
- `dust(count, centre, extent, radius=0.0016, energy=14.0, seed=7, colour=(1.0, 0.92, 0.78), name='Dust')` — Little glowing motes floating in front of the subject.
- `render(path, width, height, samples=96, engine='CYCLES', exposure=0.0, look='None', view_transform='Standard', transparent=False, denoise=True, prefer_gpu=True)` — Render the scene camera to `path`. Returns the engine actually used.
- `fit_camera_to_sequence(camera_name, object_names, frames, *, margin=0.06, target=None, max_iterations=12)` — Fit a perspective camera around an evaluated multi-frame envelope.
- `fit_camera_to_target_sequence(camera_name, object_names, frames, target_bbox_px, *, target=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), azimuth=270.0, elevation=0.0, distance=10.0, lens=50.0, resolution=None, fit_dimension='height', pose_candidates=None, shift_probe=0.01, max_iterations=12)` — Fit one perspective camera to a target envelope over several frames.
- `render_sequence(output_dir, frames, *, prefix='frame_', digits=4, width=480, height=270, samples=12, engine='CYCLES', exposure=0.0, look='None', view_transform='Standard', transparent=False, denoise=True, prefer_gpu=True, max_bounces=4, clear=True)` — Render selected scene frames as a deterministic PNG sequence.

## `mesh_audit`

Read-only structural reports for named evaluated mesh objects.

- `inspect_meshes(obj_names, *, property_keys=())` — Report evaluated structure for one or more named mesh objects.

## `meshgen`

Procedural mesh primitives: a sweeper, a lathe, a chamfered box, and the placement helpers that go with them.

- `finish(bm, name, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), smooth=False)` — bmesh -> a linked, flat-shaded object at `location`.
- `catmull3(anchors, n_per_seg=8)` — 3D Catmull-Rom through `anchors`, ends clamped.
- `tangents(points)` — Unit tangent at each point — central differences, one-sided at the ends. A zero-length segment (a repeated control point) borrows its neighbour rather than normalising a zero vector.
- `frames(points, seed_up=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0))` — Parallel-transported (normal, binormal) at each point.
- `tube(points, radii, sides=6, name='Tube', cap_start=True, cap_end=True, smooth=False, phase=0.0)` — Sweep a `sides`-gon along the 3D polyline `points`.
- `spin_profile(profile, sides=16, name='Spun', location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), smooth=False)` — Solid of revolution about Z from a list of (radius, z).
- `spin_profiles(specs, default_sides=16, default_smooth=False)` — Build a batch of named solids of revolution from profile specifications.
- `smooth_by_angle(obj, degrees=32.0)` — Smooth shading, but keep every edge sharper than `degrees` sharp.
- `bevel_box(size, bevel=0.0, segments=1, name='Box', location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), rotation_z=0.0)` — A chamfered cube. `size` is (x, y, z) FULL dimensions.
- `icosphere(bm, radius, subdivisions=1)` — create_icosphere with a fallback for the argument rename.
- `append_bmesh(bm, other)` — Copy `other`'s geometry into `bm` and free it. bmesh has no join, and building each feature in its own bmesh keeps the index bookkeeping local.
- `tube_into(bm, pts, radius, sides)` — tube() without the object plumbing, for building a feature inside an existing bmesh.
- `place(obj, location, azimuth=0.0, pitch=0.0, roll=0.0, scale=1.0)` — Put a locally-built part into the plant.
- `point_on(points, t)` — The world point a fraction `t` along a polyline, by arc length.
- `azimuth_of(direction)` — Degrees about Z of a world direction — the number `place` wants.
- `pitch_of(direction)` — Degrees above horizontal of a world direction.
- `join(objects, name)` — Join a list of objects into the first one and rename it.

## `paint`

Screen-projected linear gradient painting — mirrors Blender's own Texture Paint "Fill" tool with Linear Gradient content: you drag a line across the VIEWPORT and the gradient follows that line's direction in SCREEN space, so it looks right no matter how the UV unwrap happens to be laid out.

- `gradient_line_preview(label='grad', rows=8, cols=8)` — Render the current view + a normalized reference grid (no geometry touched) so you can read off two (x_norm, y_norm) points defining the gradient line for apply_screen_gradient().
- `gradient_line_plan_preview(point0, point1, label='grad')` — READ-ONLY. Draws the candidate gradient line (point0 -> point1, normalized image coords) on a fresh viewport render, labelled with exact coordinates. Doesn't touch geometry or the texture.
- `apply_screen_gradient(obj_name, image_name, point0, point1, value0=0.0, value1=1.0, subdiv=12, label='grad')` — Bake a grey gradient into `image_name`, driven by each point's projected position in the CURRENT view along the line point0->point1 (normalized image coords, same convention as gradient_line_preview()).
- `stroke_lines_preview(strokes, label='lines')` — READ-ONLY. Preview N candidate strokes at once on a fresh render of the CURRENT view. Each entry in `strokes` is a dict:
- `apply_paint_lines(obj_name, image_name, strokes, label='lines', face_normal=None, normal_tolerance=0.9)` — Bake N screen-space strokes into `image_name` in one optimized pass.

## `path_measure`

Read-only measurements for a batch of world-space surface paths.

- `audit_world_paths(obj_name, paths_world, labels=None, face_normal=(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), face_dot=0.55, path_radius=0.045, end_margin=None, section_half_width=0.13, section_half_tangent=0.006, thresholds=(0.001, 0.003, 0.005, 0.008), bin_size=0.001, reference_points=None)` — Measure depth and central cross-sections for world-space surface paths.

## `perceive`

Perception helpers — render an overlay for the agent to read next turn.

- `extrude_ruler(axis=(0, 0, 1), kind='screen', step=40, k_range=None)` — Render the extrude ruler overlay along `axis` from selected verts.
- `body_profile_preview(steps, direction=1, label='profile', pre_scale=1.0)` — READ-ONLY preview of a chained extrude+scale-along-local-Z profile, for building a tapered body (bat torso, etc.) from a seed cylinder.
- `scale_overlay(axis_mask, factors)` — Render the scale ruler overlay for currently selected verts.
- `loopcut_dirs(seed_loop_indices=(0, 1))` — Render the loopcut direction preview overlay for the selected face.
- `inset_overlay(px_step=12)` — Render the inset-thickness overlay for the currently selected face.
- `face_map(tl_norm=(0.2, 0.15), br_norm=(0.75, 0.85))` — Label the center of every visible face whose projected center falls inside the region.
- `face_at_label(label, prior_action=None)` — Return the face_idx for a label (e.g. "F3") from a previous face_map() call.
- `edge_map(tl_norm=(0.0, 0.0), br_norm=(1.0, 1.0), max_edges=60, visible_only=True)` — Label every mesh edge whose projected MIDPOINT falls inside the region (and is actually within the render frame) with a red line + "E_N" tag, drawn straight onto a fresh render of the CURRENT view by edge_map.py. This is the ground truth for "where is this specific edge on screen" — read coordinates off the returned payload (or the saved *_emap.png overlay) instead of computing/guessing a point's projection independently, which is easy to get backwards (e.g. a front/back Y-sign mixup) with no visual feedback until it's already baked wrong.
- `edge_at_label(label, prior_action=None)` — Return {"v0":{x,y}, "v1":{x,y}, "mid":{x,y}} (viewport pixel coords) for a label (e.g. "E_7") from a previous edge_map() call.
- `viewport_drag_dots(rows=8, cols=10)` — Render a full-viewport drag-dot grid so the agent can pick a pan target.
- `face_grid(tl_norm=(0.25, 0.25), br_norm=(0.75, 0.75), rows=8, cols=8, labels=False, style='dots')` — Render a face-selection grid over the current viewport.
- `face_at_grid(row, col, prior_action=None)` — Resolve a (row, col) pick to a face index via raycast through the viewport.
- `grab_preview(plane_axes=None, n_dots=7, px_step=40)` — Render the 2D grab destination grid on the current selection.
- `grab_line_preview(axis=(0, 0, 1), kind='world', step=0.05, k_range=None)` — Linear grab-along-axis preview — ticks at fixed spacing along `axis`.
- `grab_at(i, j, prior_action=None)` — Look up world_offset (dh, dv) for grid point (i, j) from a prior grab_preview().
- `rotate_trackball(reference_pt, pivot=None, n_dots=5, deg_step=10)` — Render the 2D trackball-rotation preview around a pivot.
- `trackball_at(i, j, prior_action=None)` — Look up (yaw_deg, pitch_deg) for grid point (i, j) from a prior rotate_trackball().
- `rotate_preview(axis=(1, 0, 0), reference_pt=None, pivot=None, angles=None)` — Single-axis rotation preview — an arc of angle ticks around `pivot` projecting where `reference_pt` would land for each rotation.
- `between_ticks(data, a, b, frac=0.5)` — World-space distance interpolated between two tick labels.
- `pick(data, ordinal)` — Look up a tick by ordinal in a ruler payload (screen, world, or scale).
- `silhouette_vs_reference(obj_names, ref_name='BatRef', label='silhouette', axis='Y', samples=48, margin=0.06)` — Draw the built mesh's outline ON THE REFERENCE PHOTO and report the fit.
- `outline_preview(obj_names, label='outline', title=None, wire=True)` — READ-ONLY. Draw what was BUILT over the reference photo behind it.
- `reference_outline(obj_names, ref_name='BatRef', label='ref_outline', title=None, margin=0.06, crop=True)` — Draw the mesh's TRUE outline on the reference photo. Red line only.

## `polyhaven`

Fetch CC0 PBR texture sets from Poly Haven.

- `info(asset)` — Poly Haven metadata for one asset id, as a dict.
- `files(asset)` — The full download manifest for one asset id, as a dict.
- `fetch(asset, maps=('Diffuse', 'Rough', 'nor_gl'), res='2k', fmt='jpg', dest='.', index=None)` — Download `maps` for `asset`. Returns {map: local path}.
- `write_credit(asset, dest, meta=None)` — Leave the provenance next to the files, not in a commit message.

## `rig`

Subject-neutral rigid IK calibration helpers.

- `solve_ik_landmarks(rig_name, constraint_name, target_name, pole_name, chain_bones, landmarks, pole_candidates, pole_angles_deg, *, seed_mode='landmarks', reset_each=True, joint_weights=None, axis_checks=(), axis_weight=0.0, selection='min_score', joint_error_limits=None, front_y_lt=None, top_n=10)` — Search a rigid IK control against measured world-space landmarks.

## `runtime`

Slim per-action helpers for BlendCUA. Hides the boilerplate every action file would otherwise repeat: sys.path setup, mem/ folder creation, checkpoint save, viewport render, status JSON write.

- `shots_enabled()` — True if per-action screenshots are currently switched on.
- `set_shots(enabled)` — Flip the cross-process screenshot toggle. Called by run.py / run_steps.py at the start of an invocation (not from inside action scripts — see the note above on why a module global wouldn't stick).
- `use(run_name, step, action)` — Initialize paths for this run/step/action and checkpoint the top of this action.
- `shot(note='', enabled=None)` — Render the current viewport for this action and write the status JSON.
- `run_dir()` — Return the current run directory (after `use(...)` has been called).
- `step_dir()` — Return the current step directory `<run>/steps/step_NNN`.
- `current()` — Return (run, step, action) tuple.

## `sculpt`

Screen-space stroke sculpting — carve damage into a dense mesh.

Worked examples and the traps: **`Tools_ref/sculpting.md`**

- `apply_carve_strokes(obj_name, strokes, label='carve', report=True)` — Carve every stroke into `obj_name`, in place. Returns a report dict.
- `carve_strokes_preview(strokes, label='carve')` — READ-ONLY path preview. Delegates to paint.stroke_lines_preview so the overlay looks identical to the painting workflow — the sculpt-only fields (width/depth/noise) are simply ignored there.
- `trim_region(world, center, normal, axis=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), half_len=0.13, lateral=0.075, irregular=0.3, seed=11, core=0.45)` — Footprint of a trim smudge. Shared by apply_trim and its preview so the two can never disagree about where the damage lands.
- `apply_trim(obj_name, normal, depth, center_world, axis=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), half_len=0.13, lateral=0.075, irregular=0.3, seed=11, core=0.45, relax_iters=3, relax_strength=0.2, rim_iters=6, rim_strength=0.3, label='trim', report=True)` — Trim brush — flatten a corner and the ground around it into a SMUDGE.

## `sculpt_native`

Blender's OWN sculpt brushes, driven from a script over the socket.

Worked examples and the traps: **`Tools_ref/sculpting.md`**

- `viewport()` — (window, area, region, rv3d) for the first VIEW_3D.
- `world_to_px(region, rv3d, radius_world, at_world)` — How many SCREEN PIXELS a world-space radius spans at a given point.
- `frame_ortho(region, rv3d, axis_dir, center_world, half_height)` — Ortho view down `axis_dir`, centred on a point, showing +/- half_height.
- `world_arrays(obj)` — (N,3) WORLD coordinates and world normals.
- `image_texture(name, path, reload=True)` — A legacy IMAGE Texture datablock wrapping a PNG on disk.
- `sample_profile(profile, n)` — A pressure value per dab, resampled to n dabs.
- `set_symmetry(x=False, y=False, z=False)` — Sculpt symmetry. X defaults to ON in Blender, which mirrors every stroke — fine for a character, wrong for weathering. Off unless asked.
- `apply_stroke(obj_name, brush, stroke, invert=False, symmetry=(False,) * 3, step_px=4.0, texture=None, label=None, profile=None, profile_size=True, **settings)` — Drag one native brush along one screen-space path.
- `apply_strokes(obj_name, brush, strokes, **kw)` — Several paths with one brush. Returns a list of reports.
- `world_path_strokes(paths_world, radius_world=None, size_px=None, center_world=None, labels=None, waviness='straight', smooth=False, show_anchors=False, color_hint=None)` — Project world-space polylines into the current viewport stroke format.
- `apply_world_strokes(obj_name, brush, paths_world, radius_world=None, size_px=None, center_world=None, labels=None, invert=False, symmetry=(False,) * 3, step_px=4.0, texture=None, profile=None, profile_size=True, waviness='straight', smooth=False, show_anchors=False, color_hint=None, **settings)` — Apply one native brush to several world-space polylines.
- `trim_box(obj_name, x0, y0, x1, y1, mode='DIFFERENCE', orientation='VIEW', extrude='FIXED', solver='EXACT', front_only=True, cursor_depth=False, label='trim_box')` — Cut a box through the model along the view axis.
- `trim_lasso(obj_name, points, mode='DIFFERENCE', orientation='VIEW', extrude='FIXED', solver='EXACT', front_only=True, cursor_depth=False, label='trim_lasso')` — Same as trim_box but through an arbitrary closed outline.
- `displace(obj_name, texture, strength, mid_level=0.5, direction='NORMAL', texture_coords='LOCAL', coords_object=None, vertex_group=None, invert_group=False, label=None)` — Push the surface along its normals by a texture. Applied immediately.
- `face_axis(name, normal, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), scale=1.0)` — An Empty whose local XY plane lies ON a face, for OBJECT texture coords.
- `drape_line(obj, a, b, direction, n=40, world=True)` — A straight line in space, raycast onto a surface — a path that FOLLOWS the model instead of cutting through it.
- `movement(before, after, mask=None)` — How far vertices moved between two world-coordinate snapshots, in mm.
- `brush_circle(center_world, radius, normal=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), n=48)` — Closed polyline of a circle, for drawing a brush footprint in previews.
- `stroke_footprint(obj, path_world, radius, hardness=0.0, tail=0.0, face_normal=None, face_dot=0.25)` — Per-vertex weights for a brush dragged along a polyline.
- `strokes_footprint(obj, paths, radius, **kw)` — One footprint covering SEVERAL paths, combined by max.
- `make_vertex_group(obj, name, weights, buckets=64)` — Write per-vertex weights as a group.
- `stroke_displace(obj_name, texture, path_world, radius, strength, mid_level=0.5, hardness=0.0, tail=0.0, texture_coords='LOCAL', coords_object=None, group='brush_stroke', label=None)` — A TEXTURED BRUSH STROKE, built out of a displacement.
- `mesh_filter(obj_name, kind='SMOOTH', strength=0.5, iterations=1, label=None)` — Whole-mesh filter: SMOOTH, RELAX, SURFACE_SMOOTH, SHARPEN, ENHANCE_DETAILS, INFLATE, SCALE, SPHERE, RANDOM, RELAX_FACE_SETS, ERASE_DISPLACEMENT.

## `section_mesh`

Subject-neutral closed low-poly forms built from measured sections.

- `make_material(name, color, roughness=0.5, metallic=0.0, specular=0.28)` — Create or update a node material from an RGB or RGBA colour.
- `assign_material(obj, material)` — Give a mesh exactly one material slot and return the mesh object.
- `rounded_section(width, bottom, top, bottom_span=0.68, lower_span=0.94, lower_z=0.1, side_z=0.32, upper_side_z=0.28, crown_span=0.8, crown_z=0.06)` — Return a clockwise chamfered/crowned 2-D section as ``(lateral, height)`` pairs.
- `loft_sections(name, stations, sections, material=None, smooth=True)` — Build a closed loft along X from caller-supplied lateral/height sections.
- `replace_closed_elliptical_loft(name, stations, centers_yz=None, radii_y=0.5, radii_z=None, sides=32, end_skew=(0.0, 0.0), skew_half='positive_y', smooth_side=True, mesh_name=None)` — Replace a mesh object's data with a closed axial elliptical loft.
- `extrude_profile(name, profile, span_axis='Y', span_start=-0.5, span_end=0.5, material=None, smooth=True)` — Build a closed prism from a 2-D profile across a named coordinate axis.
- `closed_path_tube(name, points, radius, sides=8, frame_up=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), material=None, smooth=True)` — Build a closed low-sided tube around a 3-D polyline.
- `add_bevel(obj, width=0.03, segments=2, angle=0.52)` — Replace the named angle-limited bevel modifier on a mesh object.
- `build_parts(parts)` — Build a batch of independent named forms from generic shape specifications.

## `shapekeys`

Shape-key helpers for rigid-rotation poses (wing/leg/head flap states).

- `ensure_basis(obj)` — Return the object's Basis shape key, creating it if there is none.
- `add_rotation_shape_key(obj, key_name, pivot_world, axis_world, angle_deg, vert_filter=None)` — Add a shape key that rigidly rotates part of the mesh.
- `add_bend_shape_key(obj, key_name, pivot_world, axis_world, span_axis_world, max_angle_deg, max_distance, vert_filter=None, power=1.0, min_angle_deg=0.0)` — Like add_rotation_shape_key, but the rotation angle at each vertex is GRADUATED by its distance from the pivot along span_axis_world — min_angle_deg right at the pivot, ramping up to max_angle_deg at max_distance (and staying at max_angle_deg beyond it) — a smooth curve/flex along the object's length instead of one rigid tilt for every vertex. Use for something like a wing that should visibly bend more toward the tip than right at the shoulder.
- `set_shape_key_values(obj, values)` — Set the named keys to the given values and every other key to 0.

## `simulation`

Deterministic timeline evaluation and rigid-body audit helpers.

- `configure_collision_surfaces(object_names, *, use_culling=False, use_normal=True, thickness_outer=None, thickness_inner=None)` — Set common collision flags on named mesh supports.
- `evaluate_sequence(object_name, frame_start, frame_end, *, sample_frames=None, sample_indices=(), include_final_vertices=False)` — Evaluate a mesh through every frame in an inclusive contiguous range.
- `bake_rigid_body_cache(frame_start, frame_end, *, scene=None)` — Bake the active rigid-body point cache over an inclusive frame range.
- `rigid_body_sequence_report(object_names, frame_start, frame_end, *, sample_frames=None, clear_lean_degrees=20.0, pair_gap_threshold=0.005, rotation_axis=(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), reference_axis=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), sign_axis=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0), local_reference_axis=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), floor_name=None, box_half_extents=None, child_names=None, attachment_frame=None, leave_frame=None)` — Audit an ordered rigid-body chain in one contiguous timeline traversal.
- `animation_sequence_report(object_names, frame_start, frame_end, *, sample_frames=None, reference_frame=None, centroid_regions=None, armature_name=None, chain_bones=(), bone_inventory_names=None, contact_pairs=(), binding_names=None, binding_modifier='SharkRig_Armature', binding_uv_layer=None, binding_texture_node=None, action_name=None, curve_frames=None, endpoint_frames=None, project=False, leave_frame=None)` — Audit a deforming assembly in one contiguous timeline traversal.

## `stone_texture`

Procedural stone surface: grain, pitting and colour variation for rock and masonry.

Worked examples and the traps: **`Tools_ref/wear_and_texture.md`**

- `build(size=1024, cells=9, seed=5, crack=0.05, plate_range=0.45, grain=0.22, blur_px=3, warp=0.075, amplitude=1.0)` — The height map, float in 0..1 with mean forced to 0.5.
- `write_png(path, arr)` — 8-bit grayscale PNG, written by hand.
- `build_pebbles(size=1024, cells=8, seed=3, warp=0.05, radius=0.5, radius_var=0.42, height_var=0.4, profile=1.45, aspect=0.35, floor=0.06, grain=0.1, blur_px=1, amplitude=1.0)` — A field of rounded pebbles, as a 0..1 height map.

## `wear_textures`

The texture map library that displace/stroke_displace pull from — noise, scratches, pitting.

Worked examples and the traps: **`Tools_ref/wear_and_texture.md`**

- `cracked_plates(size=1024, cells=9, seed=5, **kw)` — Broken slabs separated by dark crack lines. The general stone face.
- `pebbles(size=1024, cells=8, seed=3, **kw)` — Rounded stones sitting proud of a floor. Cobbles, aggregate, shingle.
- `pits(size=1024, cells=10, seed=7, occupancy=0.45, radius=0.42, radius_var=0.5, depth_var=0.55, profile=1.3, warp=0.06, grain=0.06, blur_px=2, amplitude=1.0)` — Scattered pockmarks eaten INTO the surface. Salt, frost, acid rain.
- `flakes(size=1024, cells=7, seed=13, levels=3, drop=0.34, bevel=0.1, warp=0.09, grain=0.07, blur_px=1, amplitude=1.0)` — Spalled terraces: a surface layer broken away in irregular plates.
- `scratches(size=1024, count=90, seed=17, length=0.22, length_var=0.7, width=0.008, width_var=0.6, angle=25.0, spread=28.0, depth_var=0.7, grain=0.05, blur_px=1, amplitude=1.0)` — Directional gouges — dragged, scraped, tooled, quarried.
- `erosion(size=1024, seed=23, base=5, octaves=5, ridge=0.75, warp=0.12, grain=0.05, blur_px=1, amplitude=1.0)` — Water-worn: rounded channels and smooth divides, no straight edges.
- `granular(size=1024, seed=29, base=14, octaves=3, contrast=1.8, blur_px=1, amplitude=1.0)` — Even coarse roughness — sandblasted, weathered, tooled.

## `weathering`

High-level weathering presets: the level an action should usually work at.

Worked examples and the traps: **`Tools_ref/wear_and_texture.md`**

- `vertical_face_lines(obj, normal, offsets, z0, z1, n=40, standoff=3.0)` — Vertical strokes on one flat face of an upright object.
- `feature_size(tile, cells, axis_scale=1.0)` — Metres per feature: one tile spans 2*axis_scale metres, and holds `cells` of them. For a map with no cell structure this returns the size of one whole tile instead, which is the only length it has.
- `axis_scale_for(feature, tile, cells)` — The Empty scale that makes one feature come out `feature` metres.
- `preview_paths(paths, radius, features=(), label='paths', note='', at=None, face_normal=None, thin=6)` — Draw the strokes plus the two sizes that decide how they will look.
- `weather(obj_name, paths, radius, layers, assets_dir, face_normal=None, face_dot=0.25, hardness=0.0, tail=0.0, axis_name=None, axis_scale=1.0, group='weather', texture_size=1024)` — Lay texture layers into the footprint of a set of brush paths.

## `wing_builder`

Small deterministic helpers for the Step 4 membrane strip.

- `positive_silhouette(obj_name, label, samples=128)` — Measure the authored +X sheet alone, without hiding it permanently.
- `outer_boundary(wing)` — Return the raw BatWing boundary edge farthest along +X.
- `extrude_outer_strip(wing, target_front, target_rear)` — Append one quad to the current +X boundary and return diagnostics.

## `lib.mesh`

bmesh selection + topology helpers.

Worked examples and the traps: **`Tools_ref/operations.md`**

- `enter_edit(obj_name, select_all=True)` — Reset Blender to a clean EDIT-mode context on the named object.
- `walk_ring(seed_edge)` — Walk the loop-cut ring containing seed_edge.
- `loopcut_at_fractions(obj, bm, ring_edges, fractions, top_z, bottom_z, from_top=True)` — Cut `len(fractions)` new horizontal rings into `ring_edges`, each positioned at an arbitrary fraction of the [bottom_z, top_z] span — unlike `bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges(cuts=N)` alone, which only ever gives even spacing.
- `selected_verts_world(bm, mw)` — World-space coords of selected verts.
- `centroid(world_pts)` — Average of world points. Returns Vector. Pass a non-empty list.
- `representative_spoke(pivot, world_pts, axis_mask)` — Pick a 'handle' vector for a multi-axis scale.
- `deselect_all(bm)` — Direct deselect via bmesh, then flush outward. No operator.
- `select_verts_where(bm, predicate, mw=None)` — Select verts where predicate(vert, world_pos) is True. Flushes inward.
- `select_verts_at_z(bm, mw, z_levels, tol=0.001)` — Common case: select all verts whose world Z matches any value in z_levels.
- `z_levels(bm, mw, decimals=4)` — All unique world-Z values among verts (sorted).
- `find_side_face_by_z(bm, mw, z_low, z_high, tol=0.001)` — First quad face that touches both z_low and z_high (cylinder side wall).

## `lib.pathgen`

Pure-math path generation for texture-paint stroke tools. No bpy — usable both from inside Blender (paint.py) and, if ever needed, from a standalone subprocess, since it's plain Python/math.

- `catmull_rom_polyline(anchors, samples_per_segment=20)` — Dense polyline through `anchors` via a clamped Catmull-Rom spline.
- `linear_polyline(anchors, samples_per_segment=20)` — Dense polyline through `anchors` via straight segments.
- `add_wobble(polyline, amplitude, frequency, seed=0)` — Offset each point perpendicular to the path by a SINGLE sine wave.
- `offset_polyline(polyline, distance, aspect=1.0)` — Shift a path sideways by `distance`, positive = left of travel.
- `add_jagged_wobble(polyline, amplitude, seed=0, roughness=1.0)` — Like `add_wobble`, but sums 3 sines at incommensurate frequencies.
- `build_stroke_path(anchors, waviness='straight', amplitude=None, frequency=None, seed=0, samples_per_segment=20, smooth=True, roughness=1.0, resolved=False)` — Anchors to a finished stroke path in one call.

## `lib.ruler`

Ruler builders. Each function returns a JSON-ready dict matching the contract documented in TOOL_AUTHORING.md.

- `screen_ruler(pivot, axis, region, rv3d, image_path, px_step=40, k_range=None)` — Ticks spaced at `px_step` pixels along `axis` through `pivot`.
- `world_ruler(pivot, axis, region, rv3d, image_path, world_step=0.3, k_range=None)` — Ticks spaced at fixed world-unit steps along `axis` through `pivot`.
- `scale_ruler(pivot, spoke, axis_mask, region, rv3d, image_path, factors)` — Ticks at world-space multiples of `spoke` from `pivot`.
- `bevel_ruler(pivot, axis, region, rv3d, image_path, px_step=40, n_ticks=6)` — One-sided screen ruler for symmetric operations like `bpy.ops.mesh.bevel`.
- `loopcut_polylines(obj_mw, ring_edges, n_cuts, region, rv3d)` — For each of n_cuts evenly-spaced fractions, project the cut polyline.
- `rotate_ruler(pivot, axis, reference_pt, region, rv3d, image_path, angles=None)` — Preview rotation angles by projecting where `reference_pt` lands after rotating around `axis` through `pivot`.
- `grab_grid(pivot, plane_axes, region, rv3d, image_path, n_dots=6, px_step=40)` — 2D grab destination grid in a world-space plane.
- `trackball_grid(pivot, reference_pt, region, rv3d, image_path, n_dots=5, deg_step=10)` — 2D trackball rotation preview grid.
- `ring_midpoints_polyline(obj_mw, ring_edges, region, rv3d)` — Project the midpoint of each edge in the ring (loop-cut direction preview).

## `lib.select`

Region-based mesh selection.

- `select_in_region(tl_norm, br_norm, mode='EDGE')` — Select all verts/edges/faces inside a screen rectangle.

## `lib.util`

Shared helpers: overlay invocation (`run_overlay`) and scene teardown (`clear_scene`).

- `clear_scene(purge=True, keep_images=True)` — Delete EVERY object and purge orphaned data — a genuinely clean slate.
- `run_overlay(script, *args, logger=print)` — Invoke an overlay script with the given CLI args, in-process.

## `lib.view`

Viewport + projection helpers.

- `get_viewport()` — Return (area, region, rv3d) for the first VIEW_3D area, or (None, None, None).
- `shot_size(region, scale=None)` — Pixel size render_viewport() will produce for `region`.
- `render_viewport(path, scale=None)` — Render the active VIEW_3D viewport to `path` at SHOT_SCALE × region size.
- `proj_fn(region, rv3d)` — Return a closure: world Vector -> {'x','y'} in image-down coords.
- `norm_to_region_px(x_norm, y_norm, region)` — Normalised image coords (0–1, top-left origin, y down) → region pixels.
- `unproject_norm(x_norm, y_norm, region, rv3d, depth=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))` — World point under a screen pick given in normalised image coords.
- `project_to_norm(world_pt, region, rv3d)` — Inverse of `unproject_norm` — world point → (x_norm, y_norm), or None.
- `viewpoint_quality(axis_world, rv3d)` — Return 1.0 when axis is perpendicular to the view direction, 0.0 head-on.
- `pan_to_norm(x_norm, y_norm, region, rv3d)` — Pan the viewport so the point at normalised image coords becomes the view centre.
- `focus_selected(area, region, rv3d)` — Centre and fit the viewport on the current selection (Numpad . equivalent).
- `fit_objects_ortho_view(area, region, rv3d, axis='FRONT', names='all', ratio=80)` — Snap to an ortho axis and auto-zoom so named objects fill ratio% of the viewport.
- `setup_axis_ortho_view(area, region, rv3d, axis='RIGHT', zoom_out=1.0)` — Set the viewport to an axis-aligned ortho view, fit all, then adjust zoom.
- `material_shading(studio=None, world=False, floor=False, axes=False, outline=False, wireframe=False)` — Viewport shading set up for judging MATERIALS rather than geometry.
- `solid_shading(shadows=True, cavity=False, light='STUDIO', floor=False, axes=False, outline=False)` — Solid viewport shading set up for judging GEOMETRY.
